The `hack/run-integration-tests.sh` script is the main entrypoint for setting up clusters and running end-to-end integration tests. It can create a KinD cluster, install Istio, deploy demo apps, deploy Kiali, and run the test suite in one command.

Prerequisites for `hack/run-integration-tests.sh`: `kind` and `docker` must be installed, `make build` is required (kiali binary required for `local` and `offline` suites), and `make build-ui` is required (Cypress must be installed for all frontend suites).

Use `hack/run-integration-tests.sh --test-suite <suite>` for full run (setup cluster + run tests), `hack/run-integration-tests.sh --test-suite <suite> --setup-only true` for setup only, and `hack/run-integration-tests.sh --test-suite <suite> --tests-only true` for tests only against existing cluster.
run full integration tests
set up test environment
run tests against existing cluster
validate end-to-end scenarios
test in different configurations

Available test suites for `hack/run-integration-tests.sh`: `backend` (Go backend integration tests, default), `backend-external-controlplane` (backend tests with external control plane), `frontend` (all frontend Cypress tests), `frontend-core-1` (frontend core test group 1), `frontend-core-2` (frontend core test group 2), `frontend-core-optional` (CRD validation and Perses tests), `frontend-ambient` (frontend tests with Istio ambient mode), `frontend-primary-remote` (frontend multicluster primary-remote tests), `frontend-multi-primary` (frontend multicluster multi-primary tests), `frontend-multi-mesh` (frontend multi-mesh tests), `frontend-external-kiali` (frontend tests with external Kiali), `frontend-tempo` (frontend tracing tests with Tempo), `local` (runs Kiali locally not in-cluster with smoke Cypress tests), `offline` (runs Kiali in offline mode with must-gather data).

The `local` test suite is recommended for local development. It creates a KinD cluster with Istio via Sail but does not deploy Kiali in-cluster, installs demo applications, runs the Kiali binary directly from $GOPATH/bin/kiali, and executes the cypress:run:smoke test suite against the locally-running Kiali.
Build the Kiali binary and frontend UI by running `make build-ui build` before running integration tests.
Set up a test cluster for integration testing by running `hack/run-integration-tests.sh --test-suite local --setup-only true`. This takes approximately 5 minutes.

Run integration tests against an existing cluster by executing `make build` to rebuild after code changes, then run `hack/run-integration-tests.sh --test-suite local --tests-only true`. This is repeatable after making code changes.

Start Kiali locally for interactive test debugging by running: `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/kiali -c hack/ci-yaml/ci-test-config-no-cache.yaml run --cluster-name-overrides kind-ci=cluster-default --port-forward-tracing --enable-tracing --port-forward-prom --port-forward-grafana --no-browser`. Kiali will be available at http://localhost:20001.

Cypress tests use Gherkin `.feature` files with `@tags` for grouping. Feature files are located in `frontend/cypress/integration/featureFiles/` with corresponding step definitions in `frontend/cypress/integration/common/`.

Run a specific Cypress test by tag using `yarn cypress run -e TAGS="@tag-name"` from the frontend directory. Common tags include @smoke, @core-1, @core-2, @crd-validation, @perses, @multi-cluster, @multi-primary, @multi-mesh, @ambient, @tracing, @offline, and @selected.

Use make targets in the frontend directory: `make cypress-gui` opens the GUI with core tests, `make cypress-run` runs headless core tests, and `make cypress-selected` runs @selected tagged tests for debugging.
The `@smoke` tag groups quick smoke tests (~30 scenarios) and is part of the `local` integration test suite.
The `@core-1` tag groups core UI tests group 1 (~130 scenarios) and is part of the `frontend-core-1` test suite.
The `@core-2` tag groups core UI tests group 2 (~155 scenarios) and is part of the `frontend-core-2` test suite.
The `@crd-validation` tag groups CRD validation tests and is part of the `frontend-core-optional` test suite.
The `@perses` tag groups Perses dashboard tests and is part of the `frontend-core-optional` test suite.
The `@multi-cluster` tag groups primary-remote multicluster tests and is part of the `frontend-primary-remote` test suite.
The `@multi-primary` tag groups multi-primary multicluster tests and is part of the `frontend-multi-primary` test suite.
The `@multi-mesh` tag groups multi-mesh tests and is part of the `frontend-multi-mesh` test suite.
The `@ambient` tag groups ambient mesh tests and is part of the `frontend-ambient` test suite.
The `@tracing` tag groups distributed tracing (Tempo) tests and is part of the `frontend-tempo` test suite.
The `@offline` tag groups offline mode tests and is part of the `offline` test suite.
The `@selected` tag is used for manual selection of tests for debugging. Add the @selected tag to a single scenario in a `.feature` file, then run `make cypress-selected` to run only that scenario.

The project includes a `.mcp.json` file at the repo root with a `cypress-debugger` MCP server that connects to the Cypress Chrome browser on port 9222. No manual setup is needed; the `cypress-debugger` MCP tools become available automatically when Claude Code loads the project.

Before using the Cypress debug browser with MCP, ensure: (1) Chrome is installed (--browser chrome requires a Chrome/Chromium binary), (2) a cluster with Istio and demo apps is running (check with `kind get clusters` for a cluster named `ci`), and (3) Kiali is running locally (verify with `curl -s http://localhost:20001/kiali/api`).
If the test cluster doesn't exist, set it up by running: `make build-ui build` followed by `hack/run-integration-tests.sh --test-suite local --setup-only true`.

If Kiali isn't running, start it using: `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/kiali -c hack/ci-yaml/ci-test-config-no-cache.yaml run --cluster-name-overrides kind-ci=cluster-default --port-forward-tracing --enable-tracing --port-forward-prom --port-forward-grafana --no-browser`.

Run Cypress with Chrome on a fixed CDP port for MCP debugging using: `cd frontend && CYPRESS_BASE_URL=http://localhost:20001 CYPRESS_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=9222 npx cypress run --browser chrome --headed --no-exit -e TAGS="@smoke" --spec "cypress/integration/featureFiles/kiali_about.feature"`.
debug cypress tests with CDP
run tests with chrome debugging
enable browser inspection for tests
debug failing test
inspect test runner state
When running Cypress for MCP debugging, use the flag `CYPRESS_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=9222` to expose the Chrome browser on a fixed CDP port so the `cypress-debugger` MCP can connect.
When running Cypress for MCP debugging, use the flag `--browser chrome` to use Chrome instead of Electron (required for CDP).
When running Cypress for MCP debugging, use the flag `--headed` to show the browser window.
When running Cypress for MCP debugging, use the flag `--no-exit` to keep the browser open after tests finish so you can inspect the state.

Once Cypress is running with the Chrome browser on port 9222, the `cypress-debugger` MCP tools (`mcp__cypress-debugger__browser_snapshot`, `mcp__cypress-debugger__browser_click`, etc.) connect directly to the Cypress Chrome instance, allowing inspection of the test runner and the Kiali app DOM.
Use the `cypress-debugger` MCP tools to inspect the Cypress test runner, see test results, passed/failed steps, and error messages.
Use the `cypress-debugger` MCP tools to inspect the Kiali UI app under test by taking snapshots of the actual DOM state, which is rendered inside the Cypress runner iframe.

Debug failing Cypress assertions by reading the step definition (in `frontend/cypress/integration/common/*.ts`), understanding the DOM selector it uses (e.g., `td[data-label="Details"]`, `data-test="namespace-dropdown"`), and using `browser_evaluate` to run the same query against the live page.
Re-run a Cypress spec via the MCP tools by pressing `Ctrl+R`: call `browser_press_key({ key: "Control+r" })` to reload the Cypress runner page and trigger a full re-run of the current spec.
Verify the CDP endpoint is reachable by running `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list`.
Pressing just `r` via `browser_press_key` does not trigger a Cypress re-run; use `Ctrl+R` instead. Clicking the spec file link and using `browser_navigate` also do not trigger re-runs.

Important: `Ctrl+R` does NOT pick up code changes. Cypress caches compiled step definitions and feature files. If you modify a `.ts` step definition or `.feature` file, you must kill the Cypress process and restart it for the changes to take effect. `Ctrl+R` only re-runs the previously compiled spec.

To restart Cypress cleanly after code changes: (1) Kill all Cypress and associated Chrome processes with `pkill -9 -f cypress; pkill -9 -f "chrome.*9222"`, (2) Wait 2-3 seconds for ports to be released, (3) Verify port 9222 is free with `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list` (should fail), (4) Re-launch Cypress with the same command, (5) After the new browser opens, use `browser_close` then `browser_navigate` to reconnect the MCP to the new browser instance.

The `browser_snapshot` tool accepts an optional `depth` parameter to control output size: depth 3-4 for a quick overview of page structure and test runner controls, depth 5-6 for a detailed view including the Kiali app inside the iframe, or no depth limit (default) for the full DOM tree (can be 50KB+, useful for detailed inspection).

The Cypress runner page snapshot contains two main areas: the test runner panel (left side) with element refs like `e13`, `e17` containing the spec name, pass/fail stats, test steps, and timing; and the app under test iframe (right side) with element refs like `f1e3`, `f1e7` (prefixed with `f<N>e`) containing the actual Kiali UI being tested.

Use `browser_evaluate` with `() => { const stats = document.querySelectorAll('[aria-label="Stats"] li'); return Array.from(stats).map(s => s.textContent?.trim()); }` to quickly check pass/fail/pending counts in the Cypress runner.

Use `browser_evaluate` with `() => { const items = document.querySelectorAll('.command-wrapper'); return Array.from(items).slice(-10).map(el => el.textContent?.trim()).join('\n'); }` to check the last 10 Cypress command log entries, which is most useful for debugging.
Use `browser_evaluate` with `() => { const el = document.querySelector('.runnable-err-message'); return el ? el.textContent : 'no error'; }` to check for error messages in the Cypress runner.

Inspect the Kiali app DOM inside the iframe using `browser_evaluate` with `() => { const iframe = document.querySelector('iframe'); if (!iframe?.contentDocument) return 'no iframe'; return iframe.contentDocument.querySelector('#target-panel-control-plane')?.textContent?.substring(0, 200); }`.
Cypress feature files are located in `frontend/cypress/integration/featureFiles/*.feature` and use Gherkin BDD syntax with `@tags`.
Cypress step definitions are TypeScript files located in `frontend/cypress/integration/common/*.ts` that implement each Given/When/Then statement from feature files.

Key Cypress selectors used in Kiali tests: `cy.getBySel('namespace-dropdown')` returns `[data-test="namespace-dropdown"]`, `cy.get('th[data-label="Name"]')` targets table column headers, `cy.get('td[data-label="Details"]')` targets table column cells, `getColWithRowText(rowText, colName)` finds a cell by row content and column name, and `a[href$="..."]` is used for link assertions with endsWith matching.
Use `gh run list --repo kiali/kiali --status failure --limit 10` with JSON filtering to identify failed Kiali CI runs by job name and branch.
Use `gh run view <RUN_ID> --repo kiali/kiali --json jobs` to extract failing job IDs and names from a specific CI run.

Extract failure details by running `gh run view <RUN_ID> --repo kiali/kiali --log --job <JOB_ID>` and piping through grep for 'failing', 'AssertionError', 'CypressError', or 'Error:' keywords; use `-B5` flag to get context around AssertionError.

Download Cypress failure screenshots from CI artifacts using `gh run download <RUN_ID> --repo kiali/kiali --dir /tmp/ci-artifacts --pattern "*cypress*"` to visually inspect the test runner state and Kiali UI at time of failure.

Map CI job names to test suites and feature file tags: 'Run frontend core 1 integration tests' → @core-1, 'Run frontend core 2 integration tests' → @core-2, 'Run Ambient frontend integration tests' → @ambient/@waypoint, 'Run frontend multicluster multi-primary' → @multi-primary, 'Run frontend multicluster primary-remote' → @multi-cluster, 'Run frontend local and offline mode' → @smoke/@offline, 'Run backend integration tests' → Go tests in tests/integration/.

To reproduce a CI test failure locally: checkout the failing branch with `git checkout <branch-name>`, run `make build-ui build`, use `hack/run-integration-tests.sh --test-suite <suite> --setup-only true` to setup the cluster, start Kiali with `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/kiali -c hack/ci-yaml/ci-test-config-no-cache.yaml run --cluster-name-overrides kind-ci=cluster-default --port-forward-tracing --enable-tracing --port-forward-prom --port-forward-grafana --no-browser &`, then run the test with `cd frontend && CYPRESS_BASE_URL=http://localhost:20001 CYPRESS_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=9222 npx cypress run --browser chrome --headed --no-exit --spec "cypress/integration/featureFiles/<failing-feature>.feature"`.

After reproducing a CI test failure locally with Cypress running on port 9222 with `--no-exit`, use the cypress-debugger MCP tools to inspect the Chrome browser, examine DOM state, and understand assertion failures; use `Ctrl+R` to re-run the test after making fixes.

Cypress e2e test files use Gherkin BDD format (.feature files in frontend/cypress/integration/featureFiles/) paired with TypeScript step definitions (in frontend/cypress/integration/common/); step definition files are globally loaded for all feature files via the 'stepDefinitions' config in package.json.

Step definition files in frontend/cypress/integration/common/ are organized by domain: table.ts for table assertions (getColWithRowText, colExists), navigation.ts for page navigation steps, transition.ts for loading state helpers, services.ts for service-specific steps, apps.ts for app-specific steps, workloads.ts for workload-specific steps, and hooks.ts for Before/After setup.

When adding a new test scenario to a Gherkin .feature file, tag it with the appropriate demo app tag (@bookinfo-app, @error-rates-app, @sleep-app) to ensure the app is installed via hooks, and tag it with the CI suite tag (@core-1, @core-2, @smoke, @ambient, @waypoint, @multi-primary, @multi-cluster) to specify which CI suite runs the test.
Use @selected tag temporarily on a single scenario during e2e test development to run only that test for faster iteration.

Before writing new step definitions for an e2e test, check for existing reusable steps: navigation.ts provides 'user is at the {string} page' and 'user is at administrator perspective'; table.ts provides 'user selects the {string} namespace', 'user sees {string} in the table', 'table length should be {int}', 'the {string} column on the {string} row has a link ending in {string}'; transition.ts provides ensureKialiFinishedLoading() and openTab(tabName); domain-specific steps exist in services.ts, apps.ts, workloads.ts.

When writing new step definitions in Cypress, use the pattern `cy.getBySel('name')` to select elements with `[data-test="name"]` (custom Kiali command), use `cy.get('td[data-label="Column"]')` to select table cells by column header, use `getColWithRowText(rowText, colName)` from table.ts to find a cell by row content and column name, use `ensureKialiFinishedLoading()` from transition.ts to wait for Kiali loading spinners, use `openTab(tabName)` from transition.ts to click tabs, and rely on `data-test` attributes on React components for reliable selectors.

Cypress tests must work in both standalone Kiali and OSSMC (OpenShift Service Mesh Console). Use `cy.request({ url: '/api/config' })` with object format instead of `cy.request('/api/config')` because OSSMC proxies API calls and only the object form allows Cypress to resolve the base URL correctly.

In OSSMC e2e tests, use `cy.intercept('**/api/namespaces')` with a leading `**` wildcard glob in the intercept pattern instead of `cy.intercept('/api/namespaces')` because OSSMC prefixes API paths via the console proxy, and the wildcard matches both standalone `/api/namespaces` and proxied `/proxy/.../api/namespaces` paths.

For Kiali navigation links in e2e tests, use `cy.get(linkSelector('/namespaces/bookinfo/services'))` instead of `cy.get('a[href*="/namespaces/bookinfo/services"]')` because in OSSMC kiosk mode, KialiLink renders `<button data-href="...">` instead of `<a href="...">`. The linkSelector utility from utils.ts builds a CSS selector that matches both standalone `<a href>` and OSSMC `<button data-href>` elements; use linkSelector with 'endsWith' for partial path matching or no pattern for any link-like element.
To check if a Kind cluster is already running before setup, run: `kind get clusters`

To run Cypress tests with debug browser, use: `cd frontend && CYPRESS_BASE_URL=http://localhost:20001 CYPRESS_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=9222 npx cypress run --browser chrome --headed --no-exit -e TAGS="@selected" --spec "cypress/integration/featureFiles/<your-feature>.feature"` This allows cypress-debugger MCP tools to connect and re-run tests with Ctrl+R.
I need to debug a Cypress test failure
How do I run a test with the debug browser?
Can I inspect the browser state during test execution?
To run Cypress tests headless for quick pass/fail without debug browser, run: `cd frontend && CYPRESS_BASE_URL=http://localhost:20001 npx cypress run -e TAGS="@selected"`

Cypress test iteration workflow: (1) Write or modify the test, (2) Run with debug browser flags, (3) Examine error messages and use cypress-debugger MCP tools to inspect state if unclear, (4) Determine if failure is a test issue (wrong selector, assertion) or code issue (feature not working), (5) Fix accordingly, (6) Re-run with Ctrl+R if debug browser open or re-launch cypress command, (7) Remove @selected tag and verify with real suite tag before committing.

To view cumulative profiler results on looped tasks, save the profiler report and pipe through: awk -F~ '{val=$2; $2="@"; a[$0]+=val} !b[$0]++{c[++count]=$0} END{for(i=1;i<=count;i++){sub("@",a[c[i]],c[i]); print c[i]}}' OFS=\~ <(cat - | sed 's/\(.*\) -\+ \(.*\)s/\1~\2/') | sort -n -t '~' -k 2 -r | column -s~ -t

The -udi (--use-dev-images) flag in molecule tests controls whether to use dev images. Set to true to test local code changes (requires building and pushing dev images first); set to false to test with latest images published on quay.io

The -hcrp (--helm-charts-repo-pull) flag in molecule tests controls whether to pull the helm-charts repository. Set to true to pull latest helm-charts from remote repository; set to false if local helm-charts repo has a branch with no remote to avoid git pull errors
For Minikube molecule tests, run: ./hack/run-molecule-tests.sh --client-exe "$(which kubectl)" --cluster-type minikube --minikube-profile ci -udi true -hcrp false -at "token-test"
For KinD molecule tests, run: ./hack/run-molecule-tests.sh --client-exe "$(which kubectl)" --cluster-type kind -udi true -hcrp false -at "token-test"
For OpenShift molecule tests, run: ./hack/run-molecule-tests.sh --client-exe "$(which oc)" --cluster-type openshift -udi true -hcrp false -at "token-test"
Molecule tests are located in kiali-operator/molecule/. Each subdirectory is a test scenario (e.g., config-values-test, token-test)
Never modify versioned operator roles in kiali-operator/roles/v2.4/, roles/v2.11/, etc. Only modify the default role
Never modify old CSV versions in kiali-operator/manifests/*/[version]/. Only modify the LATEST version

Never modify CRD files that are not in kiali-operator/crd-docs/crd/. Golden copies are in crd-docs/crd/ (source of truth). Sync changes using: make sync-crds in kiali-operator repo (this affects both kiali-operator and helm-charts repos)
Never modify generated documentation files: kiali.io/content/en/docs/Configuration/kialis.kiali.io.md and kiali.io/content/en/docs/Configuration/ossmconsoles.kiali.io.md
Never modify _output/ directories or subdirectories as they contain build artifacts and generated files

Create a separate PR for helm-charts repo with synced CRD files after creating the kiali-operator PR.
The golden copy CRD files are kiali-operator/crd-docs/crd/kiali.io_kialis.yaml and kiali-operator/crd-docs/crd/kiali.io_ossmconsoles.yaml and are the source of truth for CRD schemas.

Do not edit CRD synchronized copies directly; they are: kiali-operator/manifests/kiali-ossm/manifests/kiali.crd.yaml, kiali-operator/manifests/kiali-ossm/manifests/ossmconsole.crd.yaml, kiali-operator/manifests/kiali-upstream/[version]/manifests/kiali.crd.yaml, helm-charts/kiali-operator/crds/crds.yaml, and helm-charts/kiali-operator/templates/ossmconsole-crd.yaml.
When upgrading Go, update go.mod using 'go mod edit -go=x.y' with the target version number.
After updating go.mod during Go upgrade, run 'go mod tidy -v' to update dependencies.
After updating dependencies during Go upgrade, verify everything builds by running 'make clean build build-ui test'.
Commit and create PR after verifying Go upgrade build succeeds.
When upgrading PatternFly, check for updates using 'npx npm-check-updates -t latest -f '/^@patternfly/'' to find available versions.
After checking for PatternFly updates, run 'yarn install' from the frontend/ directory to update yarn.lock.
Commit both package.json and yarn.lock after upgrading PatternFly.
Run 'corepack enable' once before using yarn for the first time; Yarn is managed via corepack in the Kiali project.
The exact Yarn version for Kiali is pinned in frontend/package.json via the packageManager field.

When experiencing build failures in Kiali, ensure correct Go version using 'make go-check'.
When experiencing build failures, perform a clean rebuild by running 'make clean-all' followed by 'make build-ui build test'.

When experiencing cluster push failures, verify cluster accessibility using 'make CLUSTER_TYPE=minikube MINIKUBE_PROFILE=${MINIKUBE_PROFILE} cluster-status' for minikube or 'make CLUSTER_TYPE=kind KIND_NAME=${KIND_NAME} cluster-status' for kind.
For minikube cluster push failures, ensure the minikube profile is set correctly using 'export MINIKUBE_PROFILE=ci' and verify with 'minikube status -p ci'.
For kind cluster push failures, verify clusters exist using 'kind get clusters' and ensure KIND_NAME environment variable is set correctly.
When operator is not working, check operator logs using 'kubectl logs -n kiali-operator deployment/kiali-operator -f'.
When operator is not working, check Kiali CR status using 'kubectl get kiali -A -o yaml'.
When operator is not working, verify operator image using 'kubectl get deployment kiali-operator -n kiali-operator -o yaml | grep image:'.
When Molecule tests fail, ensure cluster is clean by running './hack/purge-kiali-from-cluster.sh -c kubectl' and verify no kiali CRDs remain with 'kubectl get crd | grep kiali'.
When Molecule tests fail, rebuild images using 'make CLUSTER_TYPE=minikube MINIKUBE_PROFILE=ci build-ui build test cluster-push'.
When Molecule tests fail, run with debug mode enabled by setting 'export MOLECULE_DEBUG=true' before running './hack/run-molecule-tests.sh'.
When frontend is not loading, verify backend is running using 'curl http://localhost:20001/kiali/api'.
When frontend is not loading, verify proxy setting in rsbuild.config.ts using 'grep proxy frontend/rsbuild.config.ts'.
When frontend is not loading, restart frontend dev server using 'make run-frontend'.
To get debug information, run './hack/ci-get-debug-info.sh' to collect comprehensive debugging data.
To get operator logs for debugging, use 'kubectl logs -n kiali-operator deployment/kiali-operator --tail=100'.
To get Kiali server logs for debugging, use 'kubectl logs -n istio-system deployment/kiali --tail=100'.
To check all Kiali-related resources, use 'kubectl get all,kiali,ossmconsole -A | grep kiali'.
If encountering SELinux permission errors with molecule tests, temporarily disable SELinux using 'sudo setenforce 0' and re-enable after testing with 'sudo setenforce 1'.
For local development without a cluster, use 'make build-ui && make run-backend' in one terminal and 'make run-frontend' in another terminal for hot reload development cycle.
When starting minikube for development, set CLUSTER_TYPE=minikube, MINIKUBE_PROFILE to a profile name like 'ci', DORP=docker, and CLIENT_EXE=kubectl as environment variables.
To start a minikube cluster and install Istio, run './hack/k8s-minikube.sh -mp ${MINIKUBE_PROFILE} start' followed by './hack/istio/install-istio-via-istioctl.sh --client-exe ${CLIENT_EXE}'.
